<p class="doc-kicker">About the Gateway</p>

## Overview {#overview}

DREAM Lab's AI gateway service provides API access to Large Language Models (LLMs) hosted by campus cloud providers (currently, Google). It can be used in conjunction with a coding agent (such as OpenCode or Continue) or to build custom research AI workflows.

**Note:** The gateway does not provide a web chat UI. The service is primarily oriented toward DREAM Lab workshop attendees, researchers learning AI-assisted coding, and Library staff.
:::

## API Endpoint & Supported Models {#endpoint-models}

The OpenAI-compatible API endpoint for the gateway service is:

`https://litellm.dreamlab.ucsb.edu/v1`

### Supported Google Gemini Models

| Model Name | Best For | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gemini-4-argon` | Complex reasoning & coding | Frontier model for challenging reasoning and software architecture tasks. |
| `gemini-3.8-flash` | Agentic coding | Fast, highly capable model tuned for autonomous agent execution loops. |
| `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | Low-cost inference | High-throughput model ideal for text processing and lightweight tasks. |
| `gemini-embedding-2` | Embeddings | Multimodal embedding model for vector search and retrieval. |

## Creating an API Key {#api-keys}

Anyone with a valid UCSB NetID can create a key through the **[API Key Manager ↗](https://litellm.dreamlab.ucsb.edu/dreamlab-keys)**.

```{=html}
<div class="doc-callout doc-callout--note">
  <span class="doc-callout__icon" aria-hidden="true">ℹ</span>
  <div>
    <strong>Key Policies &amp; Restrictions</strong>
    <div>
      <ul>
        <li>You may have only one active key at a time.</li>
        <li>If you regenerate a new key, your previous key is automatically disabled.</li>
        <li>Keys expire automatically after <strong>three months</strong>.</li>
        <li>Your key has an allocated budget that resets periodically. Use the key manager to view your remaining balance.</li>
        <li>Usage reflects real API expenses; requests to larger models consume quota faster than lighter models.</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Using the Gateway with Python {#python-example}

Because the gateway exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, you can interact with models using the standard `openai` Python library:

```bash
mkdir llm-example
cd llm-example
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install openai
```

Create a script (`main.py`) specifying the gateway base URL:

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

# In a Coder Workspace with a configured key, DREAMLAB_LLM_KEY is set automatically
api_key = os.environ.get("DREAMLAB_LLM_KEY", "your-api-key-here")

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=api_key,
    base_url="https://litellm.dreamlab.ucsb.edu/v1"
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain the difference between a list and a tuple in Python."}
    ]
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

Run the script:

```bash
python main.py
```

## Data Privacy & Security {#privacy-security}

```{=html}
<div class="doc-callout doc-callout--warning">
  <span class="doc-callout__icon" aria-hidden="true">!</span>
  <div>
    <strong>Data Classification Restriction</strong>
    <div><p>The DREAM Lab AI Gateway <strong>IS NOT approved</strong> for use with data classified as <strong>P3</strong> or <strong>P4</strong> under the UC data protection levels.</p></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

The service routes requests through Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform: Google will not use campus data to train or fine-tune AI models. For full compliance details, see [UC Protection Levels](https://it.ucsb.edu/security/compliance/uc-protection-levels) and Google's zero data retention agreements.

## Responsible Use {#responsible-use}

You are responsible for how you use this service and anything it generates. Verify outputs before relying on them in research. Do not use AI services as a substitute for medical, legal, or financial advice.

*"If an action wasn't permissible before AI, it isn't permissible with AI."* — UC AI Council
